consequence.statement: The GCP workload identity parameters are no longer required, so a provider configuration that omits them is accepted where it previously was not; the evidence describes no failure or removal of behaviour.
consequence.remediation: No operator action is described; review GCP provider configurations only if strict validation of the workload identity parameters was relied upon.

original.statement: In external-secrets 0.16.0 the GCP workload identity parameters become optional (i.e. they were previously mandatory to set), a change the release notes list under breaking changes.

decision.reason: [ev-0bdd4090fd7b] and [ev-ddd3e4415b88] say only that the GCP workload identity parameters become optional. [ev-c4d8a7dd4217] shows the change touches the GCP SecretStore types, the generated CRDs, the chart snapshot and the docs. That is a loosening of validation: a resource that omits these parameters can now be accepted, and nothing in the evidence says an existing resource fails, is rejected or stops being honoured. So no action-eligible kind is supported. The "BREAKING CHANGES" heading covers all 36 items in the section, including routine dependency bumps, so it is not specific to this change. A low-severity behavior-change in the review class is the cautious, supported reading.
